verdict.rationale: Attio's REST API docs describe webhooks you can register to subscribe to workspace changes, which then send real-time HTTP requests to a target URL you choose. Each request is signed via an `Attio-Signature` header, and the OpenAPI spec lists webhook endpoints for programmatic registration. Missing for 10: a documented catalog of event types, delivery/retry semantics, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Webhooks allow you to subscribe to changes that happen in Attio and then receive real-time HTTP requests to a chosen target URL to notify you of these changes.
We cryptographically sign every webhook request using your webhook secret, and include it as HTTP header called `Attio-Signature`
You can also subscribe to events in realtime using webhooks.
describing the public REST endpoints (objects, records, lists, webhooks) with schemas.
